skill.name: dependency-auditor
skill.description: Audits project dependency files and package ecosystems for known vulnerabilities, outdated packages, license issues, and supply chain risk.
skill.summary: Review dependency health, vulnerability severity, and remediation steps across common package ecosystems.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate dependency-auditing guide with no evidence of prompt injection or malicious data exfiltration. Most static findings are Markdown fence or documentation false positives, but several package-manager, scanner, CI, and Snyk commands are real execution risks that require user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Package-manager commands can modify dependency files and lockfiles.
remediation.suggestion: State that install, update, uninstall, prune, and audit fix commands require explicit user confirmation and a clean working tree.

remediation.issue: Examples mix read-only audits with remediation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Separate audit-only commands from dependency-changing remediation steps, and recommend staging tests before applying fixes.

remediation.issue: Third-party scanners and registries require network access.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose when Snyk, npx, npm, pip-audit, or other tools may contact external services or registries.

content.user_title: Audit Project Dependencies for Security Risks
content.value_statement: Dependency risk is hard to prioritize across languages and package managers. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code produce a structured audit with severity, impact, and remediation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Reviews common dependency files such as package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod, Gemfile, and Maven project files.
Classifies dependency vulnerabilities by critical, high, medium, and low severity.
Highlights outdated, deprecated, suspicious, and transitive packages for manual review.
Suggests safe upgrade paths, replacement packages, and migration checks.
Includes license compliance and package integrity sections in the audit report.
Provides CI monitoring examples for npm audit, Dependabot, and security scanning.
limitations: It depends on available scanners and vulnerability databases for current results.
It does not replace legal review for license compliance decisions.
Some remediation commands can introduce breaking changes or lockfile updates.
Manual review is still required for exploitability and business impact.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request dependency change
use_cases.description: Assess new or updated packages before merge and request safer versions when needed.

use_cases.title: Prepare a remediation sprint
use_cases.description: Group critical, high, and medium dependency fixes into practical work phases.

use_cases.title: Check an open source project release
use_cases.description: Find outdated packages, license concerns, and supply chain risks before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Basic dependency audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one package manifest and a lockfile.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this project dependency file and lockfile. List critical and high risks first, then suggest safe next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-ecosystem review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a repository has several languages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all dependency manifests in this repository. Separate findings by ecosystem, severity, and whether the issue is direct or transitive.

prompt_templates.title: Remediation planning
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when fixes need sequencing and testing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dependency remediation plan. Include upgrade order, expected breaking changes, validation commands, and rollback considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Supply chain and license assessment
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for deeper release or compliance review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a supply chain and license review. Flag deprecated packages, suspicious names, maintainer risks, package size concerns, and license obligations.

output_examples.input: Audit a Node.js service with package.json and package-lock.json.
output: Executive summary with total dependencies and overall risk level.
Prioritized vulnerability list with affected package, fixed version, impact, and upgrade advice.
Remediation plan that separates immediate fixes from staged maintenance work.

output_examples.input: Review a Python requirements file before release.
output: Severity table for direct and transitive Python package vulnerabilities.
Deprecated package notes and safer replacement recommendations.
Testing checklist for validating patched dependencies before deployment.

output_examples.input: Assess supply chain health for a mixed-language repository.
output: Ecosystem-by-ecosystem summary of outdated packages, license issues, and monitoring gaps.
Action items for CI scanning, dependency updates, and security policy improvements.

best_practices: Run read-only audit commands before applying dependency changes.
Review lockfile diffs and test updates in staging before deployment.
Document accepted dependency risks with owner, reason, and review date.
anti_patterns: Do not run automatic fixes without reviewing the generated dependency changes.
Do not ignore transitive vulnerabilities because they are indirect.
Do not add new packages without checking maintenance, license, and package size.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically fix vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest remediation commands, but users should approve and test changes before applying them.

faq.question: Which ecosystems does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers common Node.js, Python, Go, Ruby, Java, Maven, and .NET dependency workflows.

faq.question: Can it check license risk?
faq.answer: Yes. It can summarize licenses, flag restrictive licenses, and recommend legal review when needed.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Some suggested tools contact package registries or security services. Confirm networked commands before running them.

faq.question: Can it find transitive dependency issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to call out direct and transitive dependency paths when scanner output is available.

faq.question: Is manual review still needed?
faq.answer: Yes. Humans should validate exploitability, business impact, breaking changes, and accepted-risk decisions.
